title: Local annihilated representatives of annihilated germs
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $J$ quasi-coherent ideal sheaf data of finite type [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], and $F$ a quasi-coherent module sheaf [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $x\in X$ and $s\in F_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. Suppose that the germ of every ideal section $a\in J(V)$ with $x\in V$ annihilates $s$. Then there exist an open neighborhood $U$ of $x$ and $t\in F(U)$ with germ $s$, such that $a(t|_V)=0$ for every subopen $V\subseteq U$ and $a\in J(V)$.

source.place: Properties, Tag 01PO (lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), proof; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PO

proof.text: Represent s by a section on an open neighborhood using TopCat.Presheaf.exists_germ_eq, and restrict it to an affine neighborhood U. The ideal module is quasi-coherent: its construction is the kernel of the structure sheaf map to the closed-immersion pushforward of the structure sheaf; use isQuasicoherent_pushforward_of_isClosedImmersion and isQuasicoherent_kernel. Apply the existing proved private theorem Scheme.Modules.finite_sections_of_finiteType from QuasicoherentFiniteTypeAffine, accessed by a proof-only import all, directly to J.toModules and U. This gives a finite section module without a separate restriction theorem. Map its finite spanning set along the ideal inclusion to obtain a finite set g spanning J(U).

source.place: Properties, Tag 01PO (lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), proof; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PO

proof.text: For each a in g, germ_smul and hs show that a times the representative has zero germ. TopCat.Presheaf.germ_eq gives a neighborhood on which this product vanishes. Intersect these finitely many neighborhoods with U, and choose an affine neighborhood Z inside the intersection. Restriction and map_smul show that each restricted generator kills the restricted representative n. The kernel ideal of the scalar-to-section map r ↦ r • n contains the image of J(U), hence J(Z), by IdealSheafData.map_ideal and Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap. This handles the empty set of generators by the top open as the empty intersection.

source.place: Properties, Tag 01PO (lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), proof; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PO

proof.text: Apply annihilator_affine_criterion to the affine open Z and n: the preceding kernel-ideal inclusion proves annihilation by every element of J(Z), and the criterion extends it to every ideal section on every subopen. Finally germ_res_apply shows that n still represents s.

theorem annihilator_stalk_local_lift (X : Scheme.{u}) (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    [J.toModules.IsFiniteType] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (x : X)
    (s : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).obj F)
    (hs : ∀ (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U), ∀ a ∈ J.idealOfOpens U,
      X.presheaf.germ U x hx a • s = 0) :
    ∃ (U : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ U) (t : Γ(F, U)),
      F.presheaf.germ U x hx t = s ∧
      ∀ (V : X.Opens) (h : V ≤ U), ∀ a ∈ J.idealOfOpens V,
        a • F.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op t = 0
